Project intent

docs/Authority/PROJECT_INTENT.md · line 12

Read the excerpt
  11  The reference feeling is Cubase on an Atari: you sat down, ideas went in immediately, and the machine sort of disappeared. Only notes and parts to arrange nothing more. One hand on the device, attention on the music.
  12
  13  ## The workflow it serves
  14
  15  Everything in the firmware exists to serve this loop:
  16
  17  1. **Capture** — record MIDI the moment the idea happens; the music never stops.
  18  2. **Layer** — overdub and build loops fast.
  19  3. **Refine** — surgical timing/note edits to fine-tune the groove (piano roll, faders) never stopping the music.
  20  4. **Remix** — rearrange and retrigger parts in realtime; capture this jam itself as a new way of music creation.
  21  5. **Song** — massage the captured vibe with the parts at hand and tools to fix small mistakes on the fly or fine tune grooves into a finished structure.
  22

Card-backed history

docs/Guides/ENGINE_STORAGE.md · line 94

Read the excerpt
  93
  94  Each slot keeps up to **99 undo states of its own** (`kSlotDepth`); its 100th forgets that slot's own oldest step,
  95  never another slot's. The states live in two tiers:
  96
  97  - **Hot** — in PSRAM, a shared table of 99 entries across all slots (the current states included). Undo and redo
  98    among hot states are instant.
  99  - **Cold** — a descriptor in PSRAM only (revision, loop length, and per run its record sector), with the rows on the
 100    card. When the hot table is full, the oldest undo step anywhere is *demoted* to cold instead of forgotten — when every
 101    run it lists is already on the card; an unsaved one is forgotten as before. The same happens, one step every 50 ms at
 102    most, when the content pool runs low (below 1/8 of its pages). Redo steps, a slot's current state and a session's
 103    protected start are never demoted.
 104

How the looper stores undo history

docs/Guides/ENGINE_STORAGE.md · line 112

Read the excerpt
 111  Cold states are saved in the slot's state record (its cold section) and come back at boot as descriptors; the boot
 112  reads only hot states' rows. Milestones (the library) carry each slot's hot states only.
 113
 114  Diagnostics: `!ENGINE history` (`history_cold`: cold steps per slot), `!ENGINE take` (`#ENGINE,cold`: demoted,
 115  pressure; `#ENGINE,fetch`; `#ENGINE,runstore`; `#ENGINE,grain_worst` per job class).
 116
 117  ## The library file inside
 118
 119  | Area | Sectors | What it holds |
 120  |---|---|---|
 121  | Index header A / B | 0–1 | count, where the next milestone goes, the next sequence number |
 122  | Index records | 2–513 | 4,096 records of 64 B: sequence, set, stage and stage number (`SET 2 T01` on screen), parent, wall time, tempo, loop count, shortest / longest loop, place in the log, a 2-bit-per-slot mosaic |

  60  3. **Priority order: reliability first, then Phase 3 jam/arrangement capture.** Reliability means fixing known bugs *and* a verification regime (`pio test -e native` plus structured manual hardware tests) so changes stop breaking things.
  61  4. **One surface-agnostic action layer, in both directions.** GPIO and MIDI controls map onto the same actions (input), and faders/LEDs/display share one feedback path (output). Today actions live only in `MidiButtonActions` and fader feedback is coupled to `MidiFaderManager`.
  62  5. **Portability target (fall iteration): Randomwaves Drumboy Pro** — an open-source (MIT) STM32 Cortex-M7 groovebox, C++, with MIDI I/O, SD card, 5.3-inch LCD, pads, and 8 encoders. Refactoring must separate a **platform-independent core** (track/loop/slot logic, clock math, undo, note editing, gesture-to-action mapping) from a **thin platform layer** (MIDI transport, storage, display, controls, timers, PSRAM allocation — all Teensy/Arduino-specific today: `USBHost_t36`, `EXTMEM`, Arduino `SD`/MIDI, SSD1322 driver). docs/Guides/FIXED_MEMORY_ENGINE.md · line 11

Read the excerpt
  10
  11  The minimal base module is **four GPIO buttons and one rotary encoder**. Its intended role is the full core workflow without an external controller, as defined in [project intent](../Authority/PROJECT_INTENT.md). In the engine its encoder is connected (NOTE_EDIT, see [the encoder](#the-encoder)); its four GPIO buttons are not yet.
  12
  13  The active engine surface is an **external MIDI controller**. DROID's grid and four motorized faders are the reference implementation; another controller can send the same messages. The button and fader behavior in this guide applies to that MIDI extension setup. See the [README control setups](../../README.md#two-control-setups) for the distinction and controller mapping tables.
  14
  15  ## Performance workflow
  16
  17  Eight tracks each have eight slots. One track at a time records or overdubs. Select a track with channel 16 notes 60–67; select its slot with notes 50–57. An empty slot arms Record. With transport stopped, start it to begin the armed take; on a running track, a second slot press can punch in. A filled slot queues at the playing loop's end; on a stopped track it can start on the grid; with the transport stopped a press only selects it, and the next start plays it. A queued switch during a take first ends that take.
  18
  19  Record (36) short toggles record/overdub according to state. Record ends at a bar boundary; overdub ends immediately. Play/stop (40) controls the selected track. Transport (39) controls the internal clock; incoming external clock controls transport when active. Under a running external clock, transport (39) is a local stop and start instead: every track stops while the clock runs on, and the next press brings the tracks back at the next bar line; with the master stopped it does nothing. Nothing is sent back to the master. A transport start starts the unmuted tracks' selected filled slots as well as armed recordings.
  20
  21  Track double toggles mute; long toggles solo. The playing slot's short press also toggles mute. Slot double launches a filled slot at the next launch step — a queued one sooner than its loop end; on an empty slot, or a track taking, it is the short press. The launch step is global: `!ENGINE launch-q 16|8|4|bar` (default 1/16, kept in EEPROM). Slot triple redoes; slot long is [copy mode](#copy-mode). Record long clears the selected slot. Next track (37) long opens the sets browser. A long press of any button closes every window (the sets browser, the get-a-loop picker, the length popup). In the browser a double TRK moves a stage (or, on `MOVE SET TO TRASH`, the set) to the trash at once, and a triple TRK right after brings it back.

Nothing is sent back to the master. A transport start starts the unmuted tracks' selected filled slots as well as armed recordings.
  20
  21  Track double toggles mute; long toggles solo. The playing slot's short press also toggles mute. Slot double launches a filled slot at the next launch step — a queued one sooner than its loop end; on an empty slot, or a track taking, it is the short press. The launch step is global: `!ENGINE launch-q 16|8|4|bar` (default 1/16, kept in EEPROM). Slot triple redoes; slot long is [copy mode](#copy-mode). Record long clears the selected slot. Next track (37) long opens the sets browser. A long press of any button closes every window (the sets browser, the get-a-loop picker, the length popup). In the browser a double TRK moves a stage (or, on `MOVE SET TO TRASH`, the set) to the trash at once, and a triple TRK right after brings it back.
  22
  23  ### Step and bar buttons
  24
  25  In performance (not in an edit, the browser or a popup), step buttons 0–15 restart the selected track's playing slot at that 16th of the bar playing, bar buttons 17–24 at that bar of the 8-bar page playing, at the next launch step — the buttons and their LEDs name places in the stored loop, so a stored bar outside a shortened loop lights dim when it holds notes and does nothing when pressed (past the stored loop's end: modulo the loop); the screen parks the playhead there until then. In NOTE_EDIT the step buttons are the 16ths of the bracket's bar: a press selects the step's note (again: the next one stacked there), an empty step gets a 16th C4, a double deletes, and a hold is a parameter lock — the faders and the encoder edit that note while it is held, and the release keeps the change as one undo step and brings the previous selection back. Their LEDs show that bar. The bar buttons in NOTE_EDIT only start copy mode. In LOOP_EDIT, hold a step (or a bar) and press another of its kind, either way round: the range between them becomes the loop — its left end the new start, the steps / bars covered its length (16ths give odd lengths); a double press makes that one bar or 16th the loop. The buttons are absolute: they name bars and 16ths of the stored loop (its 8-bar page holding the playhead — stopped, the loop's start — and the 16ths of that bar), whatever the loop's current start, so a loop moved to bars 2–4 can later become bars 1–3. Bars past the stored loop's end make it longer. The loop's start in the stored loop is saved with the slot. Each range is part of the visit's one undo step. Each loop remembers the last two ranges chosen with the step / bar buttons (A and B, saved with the slot). NOTELEN's single press, in performance and in LOOP_EDIT, switches between them; its double press plays the whole stored loop. Each is a new undo step that keeps the edits made since; F1, F2 and the popup leave the ranges alone. Stored bars and 16ths outside the loop that hold notes light dim; the progress bar spans the stored loop with brackets around the loop.
  26
  27  ### Copy mode
  28
  29  Hold a slot (in NOTE_EDIT a bar button, or a step you do not edit while holding) for 0.6 s — its LED pulses and a COPY window opens. A short press of another slot / bar / step pastes there and closes the window (one undo step; the target flashes three times): a slot's loop into its own runs; a bar or a note replacing what is on that bar / 16th. A double press of a bar / step target merges instead, keeping the notes there; REC's / EDIT's short press chooses replace / merge first, and the target's press then pastes at once. Each pasted note then takes the NOTE_EDIT overlap rule as the causing note (a same-pitch note starting inside it hidden, one sounding into it ended at its start), within the same undo step. A bar's or note's copy holds its notes as values: copying a note, the bar buttons choose the bar its steps paste in; a track switch or a slot press re-opens NOTE_EDIT there with copy mode kept; and a target past the loop's end first lengthens the loop to the end of that bar (one undo step). Before it the track buttons reach other tracks. holding TRK, or holding the source slot again, is LOAD LOOP (the get-a-loop picker for that slot; TRK's short press stays the next track). A double press of the source clears it (a slot, or in NOTE_EDIT that bar's or 16th's notes). A short press of the source cancels; a long hold of another slot / bar / step makes that the source; a long hold of any other button closes it at once; and the window closes by itself 5 s after the last action (a track switch restarts the countdown; its bottom edge shows the time left). A paste or a slot clear selects that slot, so record's double undoes it afterwards.

 131
 132  ## One card stream
 133
 134  The store and the library share the card's single write stream. While a milestone or checkpoint writes, no slot
 135  autosave starts (it follows when the milestone is done); a slot save already on the card finishes first
 136  (`Persistence::onCard`). A fetch of a cold undo step runs after any save in progress, and no save starts during it. The library file is created only with the transport stopped, saving approved and no take open
 137  — at boot or right after `!ENGINE approve-saving` — because preallocating it is file-system work.

 365    /// the empty slot) and whether the empty slot lies below the oldest. O(states).
 366    uint8_t chain(uint8_t slot, ManifestId* out, uint8_t max, int16_t& currentIndex, bool& emptyBelow) const {
 367      const Slot& s = slots_[slot];
 368      uint8_t n = 0;
 369      currentIndex = -1;
 370      for (uint8_t e = s.oldest; e != kNone && n < max; e = entries_[e].newer) {
 371        if (e == s.current) currentIndex = n;
 372        out[n++] = entries_[e].manifest;
 373      }
 374      emptyBelow = s.emptyBelow;
 375      return n;
